planted.note: validatePayload returns null when no validator is registered (schema.js:63-68). EVENT_SCHEMAS covers ledger.post.v1 and payout.release.v1 only, while HANDLERS also routes payout.release.v2 (consumer.js:30), so v2 payouts reach the handler with an unchecked accountId, amountCents and destination.

planted.mechanism: idempotency key lets a second actor replay
planted.note: The Redis key is the producer-supplied idempotencyKey with no account or tenant component. payoutRelease.js:13-16 answers a non-fresh claim with the stored result, so a second producer that reuses another party's key receives that payout's id and destination, and can also pre-claim a key to suppress a legitimate release.

Replay re-adds parked entries with verified=1, and consumer.js:60 skips verifySignature for exactly that marker. Entries parked with reason 'bad-signature' (consumer.js:62) are therefore re-admitted as trusted by a single operator command.

applyPosting holds the balance row FOR UPDATE, refuses a posting that would take it negative and enforces the per-entry ceiling (ledger.js:20-27). The payout handler debits through adjustBalance, a raw upsert with neither check, so releases drive the balance below zero without limit.

signature.mode is 'warn' in config/default.json:21, so a failed or entirely absent HMAC only logs and the function still returns true. Anything able to XADD to the stream is treated as an authentic producer.

The memo is escaped for HTML on the write path (ledgerPosting.js:21), which is the wrong context here and never runs for parked entries anyway: the DLQ stores the raw envelope (consumer.js:62) and interpolates memo into a shell string. escapeHtml leaves $( ) and backticks untouched, so command substitution executes inside the double quotes.

An unset or unrecognised RELEASE_CHANNEL resolves to the staging profile, whose certificatePins list is empty (env.ts:25). client.ts:64 passes that list straight to sslPinning, so a release build whose channel was not stamped ships with pinning silently disabled and points at the staging API.

secureStore.putRaw refuses any key outside NON_SECRET_KEYS (secureStore.ts:22-27) precisely so credentials cannot land in AsyncStorage. persist() imports AsyncStorage directly and writes the refresh token to it, and restore() will accept that copy when the keychain read fails.

planted.class: Selection of less-secure algorithm during negotiation

escape_like neutralises the LIKE wildcards % and _ but nothing in the SQL string layer, and the escaped term is then interpolated into text(). A single quote closes the literal. The sibling search_docket in the same file shows the bound-parameter form that was meant to be used.
